title: Nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis

steps.tx: **Calcium oxalate** is essential. Calcium stones account for approximately 75% to 80% of all nephrolithiasis cases, most commonly composed of calcium oxalate (monohydrate whewellite or dihydrate weddellite) and calcium phosphate (apatite or brushite). This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **Idiopathic hypercalciuria** (24-hour urine calcium > 250 mg in women, > 300 mg in men, or > 4 mg/kg/day) is the most prevalent metabolic risk factor for calcium nephrolithiasis, managed with dietary sodium restriction (< 2 g/day) and thiazide diuretics. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **Dietary calcium** restriction paradoxically increases calcium oxalate stone formation by enhancing uncomplexed free oxalate absorption in the gut; patients are advised to maintain normal dietary calcium intake (1,000 to 1,200 mg/day) taken with meals. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice with diagnostic threshold 1000 with diagnostic threshold 1200.

steps.tx: **Uric acid stones** form exclusively in persistently acidic urine (urine pH < 5.5) where insoluble un-ionized uric acid predominates, appearing radiolucent on conventional plain radiography but readily detectable on non-contrast CT (200 to 400 Hounsfield units). This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice, reflecting urinary alkalinization.

steps.tx: Therapeutic urinary alkalinization with **potassium citrate** (targeting a urine pH of 6.5 to 7.0) is the cornerstone of uric acid stone chemolysis and prevention, while allopurinol or febuxostat is added if hyperuricosuria or hyperuricemia persists. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **Struvite stones** (infection stones, magnesium ammonium phosphate and carbonate apatite) form in alkaline urine (pH > 7.2) infected by urease-producing organisms (Proteus mirabilis, Klebsiella, Pseudomonas), producing branched staghorn calculi. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **Cystinuria** is an autosomal recessive defect in the dibasic amino acid transporter SLC3A1 (rBAT) or SLC7A9, presenting in young patients with pathognomonic flat hexagonal crystals in acidic urine, positive sodium cyanide-nitroprusside test, and radiopaque ground-glass stones. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **Medullary sponge kidney** is a congenital non-inherited malformation characterized by cystic dilatation of the collecting ducts in one or more renal pyramids, strongly predisposing to recurrent nephrolithiasis, distal RTA, and medullary nephrocalcinosis. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.
